+# Product closure for finite periodic actions
+
+## Abstract
+
+Direct products multiply fixed-point tables and preserve the finite Dold divisibility obstruction.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Fixed points of a direct product).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.fixed_count_prodMap`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.fixed_count_prodMap` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Yash Puri and Thomas Ward (2001). *Arithmetic and growth of periodic orbits*. URL: <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL4/WARD/short.tex>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For finite carriers X and Y and self-maps f and g, the n-th iterate of the direct product action (f,g) fixes exactly the Cartesian product of the points fixed by f^n and g^n. Hence its fixed-point count is the pointwise product of the two fixed-point counts.
+
+The proof is an explicit equivalence between the fixed-point subtype of Prod.map f g and the product of the two fixed-point subtypes. It uses the actual iterate identity for Prod.map, so it records the group-action product rather than merely multiplying two natural numbers.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Dold nonnegativity survives direct products).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.product_dold_nonneg_dvd`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.product_dold_nonneg_dvd` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Yash Puri and Thomas Ward (2001). *Arithmetic and growth of periodic orbits*. URL: <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL4/WARD/short.tex>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The pointwise product of the fixed-count sequences of two finite actions again has a nonnegative, period-divisible Mobius transform. This is the arithmetic shadow of the direct-product action: apply the actual orbit-counting Mobius identity to Prod.map f g and use the fixed-count product theorem.
+
+Thus Dold's obstruction is closed under products of finite cyclic actions. The result is stronger than an abstract multiplication identity because it obtains positivity and divisibility from an explicit finite dynamical realization.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Divisor-table product consumer).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.finite_table_product_dold`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.finite_table_product_dold` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Yash Puri and Thomas Ward (2001). *Arithmetic and growth of periodic orbits*. URL: <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL4/WARD/short.tex>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+If two tables are realized on finite cyclic actions through the divisors of a positive exponent M, then their pointwise product satisfies the same nonnegative and divisible Mobius conditions at every divisor of M. The table equalities are transported term by term through the finite divisor antidiagonal, giving a reusable consumer for products of periodic systems.
+

+- Truth anchor: `D5/S1/Dynamics/PeriodicOrbits/ProductClosure.fixed_count_prodMap`

+# Positive Laplace boundary kernels
+
+## Abstract
+
+Boundary limits of a positive Laplace transform obey finite Gram inequalities and spectral budgets.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Conjugate boundary limits).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.boundary_limit_conjugate`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.boundary_limit_conjugate` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a positive measure on the real line, the Laplace transform at sigma-i*t is the conjugate of its value at sigma+i*t. Consequently, if sigma times the latter transform has a limit as sigma decreases to zero, the opposite frequency also has a limit, equal to the complex conjugate.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Finite Gram positivity at the boundary).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.boundary_positive_definite`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.boundary_positive_definite` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let mu be a positive measure on the real line such that exp(-sigma*y) is integrable for every sigma>0. Fix a finite family of frequencies t(j), and suppose the limit L(t(j)-t(k)) of sigma times the Laplace transform at sigma+i*(t(j)-t(k)) exists at each pairwise difference. For complex coefficients a(j), the double sum a(j)*conjugate(a(k))*L(t(j)-t(k)) is a nonnegative real number. This is the finite Gram positivity of the positive measure carried to boundary limits, as in step (a) of Proposition 486.1: characters give rank-one Gram matrices, integration preserves positivity, and the boundary limit preserves each finite matrix inequality.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (A budget for negative boundary masses).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.same_sign_budget`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.same_sign_budget` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let t(1),...,t(n) be distinct nonzero frequencies. Suppose boundary limits exist at all pairwise differences of 0,t(1),...,t(n), and Re(L(u))<=0 at each nonzero such difference u. Suppose Re(L(t(j)))<=-c with c>0. Then n*c^2<=4*L(0)^2. Apply the finite Gram inequality to the augmented family 0,t(1),...,t(n), with a real nonnegative coefficient s at zero and coefficient one elsewhere, and optimize the resulting quadratic inequality.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (A quadratic budget in a short window).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.gap_budget`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Laplace/PositiveSpectralBudget.gap_budget` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let t(1),...,t(n) be a distinct finite family with abs(t(j)-t(k))<delta. Suppose boundary limits exist at all pairwise differences of 0,t(1),...,t(n), and L(u)=0 at each such difference with 0<abs(u)<delta. Then the sum of abs(L(t(j)))^2 is at most L(0)^2. In particular the conclusion applies in every interval of length less than delta. The off-diagonal entries vanish. Test the augmented matrix with the coefficient L(0) at zero and -conjugate(L(t(j))) at the other frequencies; when L(0)=0, use coefficient one at zero.
+
+## References

+# Contraction of the Actual Free-Root Trace Energy
+
+## Abstract
+
+A real one-Lipschitz map contracts the original free-root trace energy on the fixed golden biased probability space.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (potential).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.potential`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.potential` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary real root value c and original square-summable edge increments z, potential(c,z,p) is c plus the sum of z over all nonempty prefixes of the finite address p.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (contractedCoordinate).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractedCoordinate`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractedCoordinate` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+On a nonempty edge p, the contracted coordinate is chi(potential(c,z,p)) minus chi(potential(c,z,dropLast(p))).
+
+**Definition 1.3 (contracted).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contracted`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contracted` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a real one-Lipschitz chi, these original-edge coordinates form an element of the original edge ell2 space. Each coordinate has absolute value at most that of the corresponding original increment.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (contractLp).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractLp`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractLp` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Composition by chi in the actual G=L2(Omega,M) is defined as the actual constant chi(0) plus composition by x mapped to chi(x)-chi(0). The shifted map vanishes at zero and is one-Lipschitz, so its L2 composition is defined. The probability measure is the original phi-biased product law M.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Actual Trace Contraction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.actual_trace_contraction`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.actual_trace_contraction` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every real one-Lipschitz map chi and every F in the original free-root trace domain D, contractLp(chi,F) equals chi composed with F almost everywhere for the actual measure M, belongs to D, and has original infimum energy at most energy(F). No condition chi(0)=0 is imposed.
+
+Choose the attained least-energy extension F=constG(c)+Jz. Contract its value at every finite vertex and take differences along the original edges. The one-Lipschitz inequality bounds every new increment by its original increment, hence bounds the entire ell2 norm. Telescoping gives the contracted original potential at every finite vertex, including the freely transformed root chi(c).
+
+The actual trace of the depth projection P_h z equals the finite prefix sum along each ray almost everywhere for M. The finite edge cutoffs are cofinal among finite subsets, so the square-summable single-edge expansion proves P_h z tends to z. Boundedness of the actual J and continuity of shifted Lipschitz composition pass the exact finite-depth telescoping identity to G. Thus the contracted trace is exactly constG(chi(c))+J(contracted increments). The attained-energy comparison then proves the energy inequality.

+# The actual theta tail and a strict Robin response
+
+## Abstract
+
+The actual weighted Chebyshev theta tail equals the normalized second Mertens error and gives an explicit prefix-lcm Robin response.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The improper integral and its arithmetic consequence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ThetaTailRobinWitness.theta_tail_mertens_robin`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ThetaTailRobinWitness.theta_tail_mertens_robin` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every real x>=2 the actual function (theta(t)-t)*w(t), where w(t)=(log(t)+1)/(t²*log(t)²), is Lebesgue integrable on (x,infinity). Its negative integral is E₂p(x)-(theta(x)-x)/(x*log(x)). Here theta is the Chebyshev prime sum and E₂p is the second Mertens error with Mertens.M as its constant.
+
+Write I(x)=(theta(x)-x)/(x*log(x))-E₂p(x). Classical finite Abel summation gives I(u)=I(x)-integral_x^u (theta(t)-t)*w(t) dt. The finite calculation reuses the canonical ThetaTailPartialSummation.theta_tail_finite supplier from MertensCumulativePeak; its reciprocal logarithmic weight and prime-cutoff identities provide the finite bridge. The elementary bound 0<=theta(u)<=u*log(4), together with |E₂p(u)|<=(log(4)+6+Mertens.E₁)/log(u), proves I(u) tends to zero. ActualThetaTailLaplace supplies unconditional integrability of the same actual kernel. Taking the upper limit to infinity therefore fixes the normalization and proves the equality.
+
+For x>=10000, suppose this negative integral exceeds 7/sqrt(x). The Mertens correction E₃(x)+E₂p(x) has absolute value at most 4/x<=1/sqrt(x), and (psi(x)-theta(x))/(x*log(x))<=2/sqrt(x). These bounds give E₃(x)<-4/sqrt(x)-(psi(x)-x)/(x*log(x)). The common prefix-lcm response in LcmRobinResponse applies at this same real x.
+
+The resulting integer is exactly D=lcm(1,...,floor(x)). It satisfies D>5040, sigma(D)/D>exp(gamma)*log(log(D)), log(D)=psi(x), and D<=exp(x*log(x)), where gamma is the real Euler constant. This theorem takes the stated actual tail peak as a premise; the following application supplies it conditionally from a genuine zeta zero.
+
+Suppose rho is a complex number with zeta(rho)=0 and 1/2<beta=Re(rho)<1. Then for every natural number B there is a real x>=10000 such that the actual integer D=lcm(1,...,floor(x)) satisfies B<D, 5040<D, sigma(D)/D>exp(gamma)*log(log(D)), log(D)=psi(x), and D<=exp(x*log(x)). This is an application of CriticalThetaTailPeak.critical_theta_tail_peak, ActualThetaTailLaplace.actual_theta_tail_laplace_ode and the arithmetic theorem above, with the same actual theta tail and the same prefix-lcm integer throughout.
+
+To derive the application, let m be analyticOrderNatAt(zeta,rho) and A=m/(norm(rho)*norm(rho-1)). The critical peak theorem gives m>0; the real-part bounds exclude rho=0 and rho=1, so A>0. Set c=A/2 and delta=beta-1/2>0. The Mathlib limit tendsto_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_atTop_nhds_zero at exponent one gives 7*u*exp(-delta*u) tending to zero. Choose a threshold beyond which this quantity is less than c, and choose U also beyond 1, log(10000) and log(B+1). The genuine-zero critical peak theorem supplies u>max(U,log(2)) with c<u*exp((1-beta)*u)*f(u). Since u*exp((1-beta)*u)>0 and its product with 7*exp(-u/2) is exactly 7*u*exp(-delta*u), this forces f(u)>7*exp(-u/2). The actual change-of-variables identity f(u)=F(exp(u)), where F is the negative weighted theta integral, and sqrt(exp(u))=exp(u/2) give F(x)>7/sqrt(x) at x=exp(u)>=10000. The theorem above now gives the strict Robin inequality, exact logarithm and original size bound at this x.
+
+The choice x>=B+1 gives B+1<=floor(x). For n=floor(x)>=1, Chebyshev.choose_dvd_lcmUpto gives n dividing lcmUpto(n); positivity of lcmUpto(n) then gives n<=D, hence B<D. Thus the selected-zero conclusion concerns unbounded genuine integers, without an additional assumed tail peak.
+
+The complete contrapositive application assumes only that RiemannHypothesis is false. For every natural B it yields a real x>=10000 with the same actual D=lcm(1,...,floor(x)), B<D, 5040<D, sigma(D)/D>exp(gamma)*log(log(D)), log(D)=psi(x), and D<=exp(x*log(x)). To prove this, suppose there is no such witness for a chosen B. The selected-zero application then excludes every zeta zero in 1/2<Re(rho)<1. The existing RightHalfStripRiemannReduction.golden_right_half_strip_implies_rh gives RH, contradicting the premise. That supplier already handles reflection and trivial-zero classification; the application needs no rightmost zero, assumed theta error bound, extra integrability premise or extra peak premise.
+
+Consequently, an eventual nonstrict Robin upper bound on this actual family suffices for RH: if there exists a natural B such that for every real x>=10000, B<lcmUpto(floor(x)) implies sigma(D)/D<=exp(gamma)*log(log(D)) at D=lcmUpto(floor(x)), then RiemannHypothesis holds. For each right-half-strip zero the selected-zero application at that same B supplies a strict violation at a family member to which the upper bound applies, a contradiction. The same right-half-strip reduction therefore gives RH.
+
+These two complete applications are compiled specializations of the named theta-tail arithmetic theorem and the existing suppliers, rather than additional named theorems in this module. They assert conditional implications; they do not prove RH, its converse family bound, the existence of an off-line zero, an actual numerical Robin counterexample, or an effective cutoff or location for the witnesses.
+

+
+## Abstract
+
+A one-factor positive instance refutes the unrestricted signed product congruence.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The inclusive signed binomial-product sum).**
+
+$$\forall r \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall m \in \operatorname{IntVector}\left(r\right),\; \forall M \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{U}\left(m, M, n\right) = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Icc}\left(0, M \cdot n\right)} {\operatorname{Product}\left(i, \operatorname{Fin}\left(r\right), \operatorname{RingChoose}\left(\operatorname{m}\left(i\right) \cdot \operatorname{NatCast}\left(n\right), k\right)\right)}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ArithSums/A397436GeneralSupercongruenceRefutation.U` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; OEIS Foundation Inc. (2026). *OEIS A397436 revision 44, Conjecture 3 on integer-parameter binomial products*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A397436/internal>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For natural r, m is a function Fin r to the integers. Ring.choose is the generalized binomial on integer upper arguments, including negative values. The sum includes k=0 and k=M*n; the product runs over all r indices. NatCast embeds n into the integers before multiplication by m(i). No zero-for-negative-upper convention is used.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The full same-r universal assertion).**
+
+$$\forall r \in \mathbb{N},\; 0 < r \Rightarrow \left(\forall m \in \operatorname{IntVector}\left(r\right),\; \forall M \in \mathbb{N},\; 0 < M \Rightarrow \left(\forall p \in \mathbb{N},\; \left(\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right) \land 5 \le p\right) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Divides}\left(\operatorname{NatCast}\left(p\right)^{3 \cdot r}, \operatorname{U}\left(m, M, p^{r}\right) - \operatorname{U}\left(m, M, p^{\operatorname{NatSub}\left(r, 1\right)}\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/ArithSums/A397436GeneralSupercongruenceRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Peter Bala; OEIS Foundation Inc. (2026). *OEIS A397436 revision 44, Conjecture 3 on integer-parameter binomial products*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A397436/internal>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+IntVector(r) means Fin r to the integers; Prime is natural primality. The same positive r controls factor count, both lifting exponents and the exponent 3*r of the modulus. NatSub is natural subtraction; r>0 makes r-1 the source exponent. M is any positive natural and m is unrestricted. This encodes the literal item 3, with no restrictions imported from items 1 or 2.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The universal assertion is false).**
+
+$$\neg claim$$
+

+# Three same-sign SMALL labels, including adjacency
+
+## Abstract
+
+Forward physical completion with exactly three same-sign SMALL occurrences
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (One complete physical word with forward LARGE cyclic order).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/ThreeSmallSameSignSource.actualSource_three_small_same_sign_full_completion`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/ThreeSmallSameSignSource.actualSource_three_small_same_sign_full_completion` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let k>=3 and t be arbitrary natural numbers, f(i)=SourceWidth.actualSource(k,t,i), N=2^k-1, Q=2^(k-2), and C=half(k)=(N-1)/2. Suppose exactly three physical labels satisfy |f(i)|<Q and all such values are nonnegative, or all are nonpositive. There exists one list L of Fin(k) labels which permutes List.ofFn(id), is Nodup, has toFinset equal to univ, satisfies InStrip(f,C,0,L), has mass zero, and satisfies the native Legal(k,t,L). For every natural n, including takes beyond the full length, 0<=mass(f,L.take(n))<=C. The LARGE filter of this same L is List.IsRotated to the LARGE filter of List.finRange(k). No coprimality, numerical injectivity, minimal period, isolation, supplied placement, or total-zero hypothesis is required. Repeated values retain their distinct physical labels.
+
+A zero at one label propagates to the complete native row, so the forward inventory itself is a completion in that case. Otherwise orient the common SMALL sign positively and choose a minimum positive SMALL value as the physical origin. The other SMALL labels occur at forward offsets p and r. The original large_gap_profile, applied to each of the three actual gaps and its positive endpoint, forces the intervening LARGE counts to be 2A,2B,2D. Thus p=2A+1, r=2A+2B+2 and k=2A+2B+2D+3. All of these data are extracted from the native count and seam recurrence, rather than assumed.
+
+Work in sixfold integer units. With F=4^A, G=4^B, H=4^D, let d=N-6w(0), e=N-6w(p), z=N-6w(r). The cyclic endpoint equations are 2Fd=N+e, 2Ge=N+z and 2Hz=N+d. Since N=8FGH-1 they give d=4GH+2H+1, e=4HF+2F+1 and z=4FG+2G+1. Choosing the least SMALL value makes d the greatest deficit. A block with deficit d has pair values 2N-2*4^j*d and -2N-4*4^j*d. From initial height h its valleys are h+2d-2*4^j*d and its peaks are h+2N+2d-4*4^j*d. The existing paired_segment induction, monotonicity and endpoint bounds control every physical step. A sixfold height at most 3N gives the sharp unscaled integer bound C.
+
+If only the Z block is nonempty, the word is beta, the first D-1 Z pairs, alpha, gamma, then the last Z pair. If Y and Z are nonempty and A=0, start at beta and insert alpha before the last Y pair when e<=z, or after the whole Y block when z<e; insert gamma immediately before the last Z pair. These words also cover empty initial segments. With all blocks nonempty choose the least Y cut jY with d<=4^jY*e. Choose the Z cut explicitly from jZ=max(1,D-A). The closed deficits and maximality of d imply 1<=jZ<=D and d<=4^jZ*z<=2(d+z). Place beta, all X pairs, the first jY-1 Y pairs, alpha, the remaining Y pairs, the first jZ-1 Z pairs, gamma, and the remaining Z pairs. The inequalities on both sides of each cut bound the valleys below and peaks above; the cyclic endpoint equations give final height zero. Every physical position occurs once. In every branch deleting the three SMALL labels leaves precisely the consecutive X, Y and Z arcs in forward order.
+
+The physical phase map is addition by the chosen origin in the cyclic group Fin(k). It transports the normalized inventory to the actual labels and sends the native forward inventory to a cyclic rotation. Filtering commutes with that map. For negative orientation the original negate_rotation theorem cuts the positive strip word at an extremum and negates the weights; prefix heights stay in the same strip, with no reversal of physical order. Filtering this final cyclic cut preserves the whole forward LARGE cycle. The group action transports occurrences rather than numerical values, so the argument includes nonunits and proper numerical periods.
+
+The source context is Damasdi, Frankl, Pach and Palvolgyi, Monochromatic configurations on a circle, arXiv:2504.10687v2, Conjecture 3.1, DOI 10.5070/C6.68671. This construction treats the complete exactly-three, same-sign SMALL subcase with adjacency. Mixed SMALL signs, arbitrary SMALL counts with adjacency, and full Conjecture 3.1 remain open.

+# The Subgraph Core and Native Blocks
+
+## Abstract
+
+The entire maximizing set of actual connected-subgraph counts lies in one block.
+
+Dinesh Pandey and Kamal Lochan Patra, Some new central parts of connected graphs, arXiv:2110.00738v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00738v1, page 9, state: Conjecture 3.25. The subgraph core of a graph G is contained in a block of G. Definition 3.23 on that page counts connected subgraphs containing a vertex. Page 1 specifies finite simple connected undirected graphs, defines a cut vertex by disconnection after deletion, and defines a block as a maximal subgraph with no cut vertex.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Actual vertex and edge choices).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphNumber`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphNumber` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite simple graph G and vertex v, subgraphNumber(G,v) is the cardinality of the actual connected subgraphs containing v. It uses countContaining(G,{v}) from DePatraBridge. Each subgraph has its own vertex set and edge set. Distinct edge choices are distinct objects, inducedness is not required, and singleton subgraphs are included.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The entire maximizing set).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphCore`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphCore` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A vertex v belongs to subgraphCore(G) precisely when subgraphNumber(G,w) is at most subgraphNumber(G,v) for every vertex w of G.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Maximal connected subgraphs without a cut vertex).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.NativeBlock`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.NativeBlock` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+NoCut(H) means that H is connected and deleting any one vertex leaves no pair of mutually unreachable remaining vertices. Deletion restricts both the actual vertex set and the actual edges. NativeBlock(H) means maximality for NoCut under subgraph inclusion, including both vertices and edges. Empty deletion has no disconnected pair. Thus a one-vertex graph has its singleton block, and a bridge edge is admitted as a block. No order cutoff is imposed.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (One block contains all maximizers).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/pandey-patra-2021-subgraph-core` (proved) by `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"pandey-patra-2021-subgraph-core","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Citation.* Dinesh Pandey; Kamal Lochan Patra (2021). *Some new central parts of connected graphs*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00738v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite vertex type V and every connected simple graph G on V, there exists a native block B of G with subgraphCore(G) contained in B.verts. The block is shared by the entire maximizing set.
+
+The counting argument extends a connected subgraph H containing x and omitting r along a path from r to x, stopping at its first encounter with H. Let L be the path before that encounter and K the union of the path with H. Then K contains r and x, L contains r and omits x, and deleting L's vertices from K recovers H, including its edge choices. This injects the x-only subgraphs into pairs consisting of an r-and-x subgraph and an r-only subgraph. Writing d for the former count and a for all r-containing subgraphs gives the bound c <= d(a-d) for the x-only count c.
+
+At a one-vertex separation with root r, write a and b for the local root counts on the two sides, and d and e for the local joint counts at r,x and r,y. Exact gluing gives f(r)=ab, f(x)=c+db and f(y)=h+ea. The path-extension bound gives c <= d(a-d) and h <= e(b-e). The root singletons give d<a and e<b. If both f(x) and f(y) were at least f(r), these inequalities would force b<=d<a<=e<b, a contradiction. Hence maximizers different from r cannot lie in different components after deleting r.
+
+For a maximizing set with at least two vertices, take the union of all simple paths between maximizing vertices. Every vertex on such a path, after deleting a vertex z, can still reach one endpoint different from z along that path. All maximizing vertices different from z are mutually reachable after deleting z by the separation argument, and their connecting simple paths belong to the same union. The induced graph on this union therefore has no cut vertex. A singleton maximizing set starts with its singleton subgraph. Finiteness extends either subgraph to a maximal one.
+

+# A Path Hull Without Cut Vertices
+
+## Abstract
+
+Vertex inseparability produces a connected subgraph without cut vertices.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (A common cover for an unseparated set).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreHull.exists_no_cut_cover`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreHull.exists_no_cut_cover` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let G be a connected simple graph and S a nonempty set of vertices. Suppose that for every deleted vertex z, every two members of S different from z remain mutually reachable in G-z. There exists a connected subgraph H containing the entire set S such that deleting any vertex from H leaves no pair of mutually unreachable remaining vertices. No finiteness or lower bound on the order is needed.
+
+Take every vertex on any simple path with both endpoints in S, and induce a subgraph on this union. The trivial paths include S. If a vertex x in the union differs from a deleted vertex z, at least one of the two segments from x to its path endpoints avoids z, because the path has no repeated vertex. Thus x can reach a surviving endpoint in S. The hypothesis connects any two surviving endpoints after deletion, and a simple path between them is itself included in the union. Concatenating these paths proves the required reachability. For a singleton S, the union is a singleton; deleting its sole vertex leaves no pair to disconnect.
+
+## References
+

+# Positive coefficients of the five-data Newton sums
+
+## Abstract
+
+Strict positive monomial coefficients give the rational shifted generating function and the positive-index recurrence for A301420.
+
+All series have rational coefficients. Fin(5) is indexed by i = 0,1,2,3,4; its coordinate i has weight i+1. Positive sequence indices belong to N with zero excluded. X is the series variable, C embeds rational constants, and the inverse is the formal multiplicative inverse. The formal log is log(1+X); subst(p,f) substitutes p into f, and rescale(c,f) replaces X by cX.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Multiplicity vectors).**
+
+$$Multiplicity = \operatorname{Fin}\left(5\right)\to\mathbb{N}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/PowerSeries/PositiveNewtonSums.Multiplicity` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Gregory Gerard Wojnar (2018). *OEIS A301420: positive coefficients of five-data generalized Chebyshev polynomials*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A301420>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A vector records one nonnegative multiplicity for each of the five distinct monomial variables.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Factor count).**
+
+$$\forall m \in Multiplicity,\; \operatorname{count}\left(m\right) = \sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}\left(5\right)}(\operatorname{m}\left(i\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/PowerSeries/PositiveNewtonSums.count` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Gregory Gerard Wojnar (2018). *OEIS A301420: positive coefficients of five-data generalized Chebyshev polynomials*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A301420>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The total number r of factors is the unweighted sum of the five multiplicities.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Weighted degree).**
+
+$$\forall m \in Multiplicity,\; \operatorname{degree}\left(m\right) = \sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}\left(5\right)}(\left(i + 1\right) \cdot \operatorname{m}\left(i\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/PowerSeries/PositiveNewtonSums.degree` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Gregory Gerard Wojnar (2018). *OEIS A301420: positive coefficients of five-data generalized Chebyshev polynomials*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A301420>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The five weights are one through five. The factor count is at most this weighted degree.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Monomials of a fixed degree).**
+
+$$\forall k \in \mathbb{N},\; \forall m \in Multiplicity,\; m\in\operatorname{multiplicities}\left(k\right)\iff\operatorname{degree}\left(m\right) = k$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/PowerSeries/PositiveNewtonSums.multiplicities` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Gregory Gerard Wojnar (2018). *OEIS A301420: positive coefficients of five-data generalized Chebyshev polynomials*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A301420>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The finite set is the union over r from zero through k of the r-factor antidiagonals, filtered by weighted degree k. Membership is equivalent to degree(m)=k, so every multiplicity vector occurs once.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (The literal Girard-Waring coefficient).**
+
+$$\forall k \in (\mathbb{N})^{+},\; \forall m \in Multiplicity,\; \operatorname{literalCoefficient}\left(k, m\right) = \frac{k}{5 \cdot \operatorname{count}\left(m\right)} \cdot \frac{\operatorname{factorial}\left(\operatorname{count}\left(m\right)\right)}{\prod_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}\left(5\right)}(\operatorname{factorial}\left(\operatorname{m}\left(i\right)\right))} \cdot \prod_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}\left(5\right)}((\operatorname{choose}\left(5, i + 1\right))^{\operatorname{m}\left(i\right)}) \cdot (-1)^{k + \operatorname{count}\left(m\right)}$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/PowerSeries/PositiveNewtonSums.literalCoefficient` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Gregory Gerard Wojnar (2018). *OEIS A301420: positive coefficients of five-data generalized Chebyshev polynomials*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A301420>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Equation (2) of Wojnar, Wojnar and Brin, arXiv:1706.08381v2, pp. 3-4, gives this normalized five-data coefficient. For a vector of degree k its factor count is positive. The coefficient is attached to a monomial before data values are substituted.
+

+# A rational six-axis open cover
+
+## Abstract
+
+Six explicit rational axes cover the real unit two-sphere by relatively open orthogonality-free sets.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Real Euclidean three-space).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.Space`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.Space` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The ambient space is EuclideanSpace over the reals indexed by Fin 3, with its standard Euclidean norm and inner product.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The standard unit two-sphere).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.UnitSphere`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.UnitSphere` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The carrier is Metric.sphere zero one in EuclideanSpace over the reals indexed by Fin 3. It has the ordinary subspace topology and the standard real inner product.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The six rational axes).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.axis`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.axis` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In order, the six vectors are (1,2,0), (1,-2,0), (0,1,2), (0,1,-2), (2,0,1), and (-2,0,1). Each has squared Euclidean norm five. No normalization or choice of an irrational coordinate is required.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Strict projection superlevels).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.color`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.color` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each index i in Fin 6, the corresponding subset consists of all actual unit vectors x satisfying 5 < 2 times the square of the inner product of x with axis i. These are subsets of the entire sphere.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (An open orthogonality-free cover).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.rational_six_axis_open_cover`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.rational_six_axis_open_cover` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+All six subsets are open in the sphere, each excludes every orthogonal pair of unit vectors, and their indexed union is the entire sphere. Openness follows from continuity of the inner product and the strict inequality. For orthogonal unit x and y, the two-vector Bessel inequality gives the sum of their squared projections onto any one axis at most five; membership of both would make that sum greater than five. The proof uses Mathlib's Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le. For coverage put a=abs(x0), b=abs(x1), c=abs(x2), Q=a squared plus b squared plus c squared, and M=max(a+2b,b+2c,c+2a). Write u=M-a-2b, v=M-b-2c, and w=M-c-2a. All these quantities are nonnegative. The exact identity is 3 M squared - 9 Q = uv+vw+wu+6(aw+bu+cv)+((a-b) squared+(b-c) squared+(c-a) squared)/2. Thus M squared is at least 3 Q. One of the two signed forms for each coordinate pair has squared value (abs(s)+2 abs(t)) squared. Since Q=1 on the sphere, one of the six squared projections is at least three, which satisfies the strict threshold. This supplies the upper bound six for Feldman--Wilce Question 3. It proves no lower bound and does not determine higher-dimensional covering numbers. Feldman--Wilce supplies the question. The six-set upper bound has classical antecedents in antipodal icosahedral coverings, including Fowler, Tarnai and Gáspár, From circle packing to covering on a sphere with antipodal constraints (2002), DOI 10.1098/rspa.2002.0990. The rational coordinates and polynomial certificate describe this repository implementation; no mathematical novelty or priority is claimed.
+

+# Polygon and three-time inequalities are insufficient
+
+## Abstract
+
+Six-time pair probabilities satisfy the polygon and three-time inequalities without admitting a joint distribution.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Real pair tables).**
+
+$$\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.PairTables}\left(n\right) = \left((\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)) \to ((\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)) \to ((\operatorname{Bool}) \to ((\operatorname{Bool}) \to (\mathbb{R}))))\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Contextuality/LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.PairTables` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* J. J. Halliwell; C. Mawby (2019). *Fine's theorem for Leggett-Garg tests with an arbitrary number of measurement times*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04865v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a natural number n, PairTables n is the type of real arrays indexed by two times and two Boolean outcomes. The sign of true is 1 and the sign of false is -1, using the real-valued function sgn. Only entries with i < j constrain the probability conditions below; the array also assigns values to the other entries. The dichotomic pairwise setting is described in the source's TeX lines 148-159.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Compatible pair probabilities).**
+
+$$\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (p: \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.PairTables}\left(n\right)), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.IsPairFamily}\left(p\right)) \Leftrightarrow ((\forall (i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), ((i < j) \Rightarrow ((\forall (a: \operatorname{Bool}), (\forall (b: \operatorname{Bool}), ((0: \mathbb{R}) \le p\left(i, j, a, b\right)))) \land (\sum_{(a: \operatorname{Bool})} (\sum_{(b: \operatorname{Bool})} (p\left(i, j, a, b\right))) = (1: \mathbb{R})))))) \land (\exists (m: (\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)) \to ((\operatorname{Bool}) \to (\mathbb{R}))), (\forall (i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), ((i < j) \Rightarrow ((\forall (a: \operatorname{Bool}), (\sum_{(b: \operatorname{Bool})} (p\left(i, j, a, b\right)) = m\left(i, a\right))) \land (\forall (b: \operatorname{Bool}), (\sum_{(a: \operatorname{Bool})} (p\left(i, j, a, b\right)) = m\left(j, b\right)))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Contextuality/LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.IsPairFamily` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* J. J. Halliwell; C. Mawby (2019). *Fine's theorem for Leggett-Garg tests with an arbitrary number of measurement times*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04865v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Each table at i < j has nonnegative entries summing to one. A single family m of one-time marginals gives both the row and column sums of every such table, so shared times have the same marginal in all pairs. This expresses the compatibility condition in TeX lines 150-153 and the nonnegative pairwise probabilities assumed in Section 4.B, line 551. There is no condition on i >= j.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The pair correlation).**
+
+$$\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (p: \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.PairTables}\left(n\right)), (\forall (i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), (\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.corr}\left(p, i, j\right) = \sum_{(a: \operatorname{Bool})} (\sum_{(b: \operatorname{Bool})} (\operatorname{D5.S3.Combinatorics.IsingUniquenessSets.sgn}\left(a\right) \cdot \operatorname{D5.S3.Combinatorics.IsingUniquenessSets.sgn}\left(b\right) \cdot p\left(i, j, a, b\right)))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Contextuality/LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.corr` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* J. J. Halliwell; C. Mawby (2019). *Fine's theorem for Leggett-Garg tests with an arbitrary number of measurement times*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04865v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The real correlation is the sum of the product of the two signs weighted by their pair-table entry. This is the correlator in TeX lines 155-159. The definition applies to every pair of indices, including those outside i < j.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The n-gon inequalities).**
+
+$$\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (p: \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.PairTables}\left(n\right)), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.NGonInequalities}\left(p\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\forall (s: (\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)) \to (\operatorname{Bool})), (\operatorname{ite}\left(\operatorname{Odd}\left(n\right), (1: \mathbb{R}), (0: \mathbb{R})\right) \le (\operatorname{Nat.cast}\left(n\right): \mathbb{R}) + (2: \mathbb{R}) \cdot \sum_{(i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right))} (\sum_{(j: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right))} (\operatorname{ite}\left(i < j, \operatorname{D5.S3.Combinatorics.IsingUniquenessSets.sgn}\left(s\left(i\right)\right) \cdot \operatorname{D5.S3.Combinatorics.IsingUniquenessSets.sgn}\left(s\left(j\right)\right) \cdot \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Contextuality.LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.corr}\left(p, i, j\right), (0: \mathbb{R})\right)))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Contextuality/LeggettGargSixTimeSufficiencyRefutation.NGonInequalities` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* J. J. Halliwell; C. Mawby (2019). *Fine's theorem for Leggett-Garg tests with an arbitrary number of measurement times*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.100.042103). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04865v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every Boolean sign assignment s, the signed sum of pair correlations obeys the polygon bound of Section 4.A, equation (neweq), TeX lines 494-512. The lower bound is one for odd n and zero for even n. The natural number n is cast to a real number in the right-hand side. The double sum includes exactly the terms with i < j.
+

+## Abstract

+# Three-state overlap intervals need not be tight
+
+## Abstract
+
+Five overlaps of four pure states force the sixth to be one quarter, although intersection of the three-state lower bounds gives zero.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The three-state upper bound).**
+
+$$\forall \left(x: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\forall \left(y: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.upper}\left(x, y\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \left(\operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(x\right) \cdot \left(y\right)\right) + \operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - x\right) \cdot \left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - y\right)\right)\right)^{\left(2: \mathbb{N}\right)}\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.upper` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For real x and y, upper is the square of the sum of the two square roots. For known pure-state overlaps in the unit interval, this is the upper bound in overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 118–122. The definition is a total real function and does not assume that its arguments lie in that interval.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The three-state lower bound).**
+
+$$\forall \left(x: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\forall \left(y: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.lower}\left(x, y\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(\left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) < x + y\right), \left(\operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(x\right) \cdot \left(y\right)\right) - \operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - x\right) \cdot \left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - y\right)\right)\right)^{\left(2: \mathbb{N}\right)}, \left(0: \mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.lower` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The lower bound is the square of the difference of the two square roots when x + y is strictly greater than one, and zero otherwise, including x + y = 1. This is the piecewise bound in overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 125–131, extended as a total function on all real arguments.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Squared overlap of two vectors).**
+
+$$\forall \left(n: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(u: \operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(v: \operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.overlap}\left(u, v\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \left(\left\lVert \operatorname{inner}\left(\mathbb{C}, u, v\right) \right\rVert\right)^{\left(2: \mathbb{N}\right)}\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.overlap` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The overlap is the squared norm of the complex inner product of u and v in the n-dimensional complex Euclidean space. For unit vectors this is the pure-state overlap of overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 97–102. The definition itself imposes no normalization condition and includes dimension zero.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Realizing the given pairs).**
+
+$$\forall \left(n: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(\psi: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.realizes}\left(i_{0}, j_{0}, r, \psi\right)\right) \Leftrightarrow \left(\left(\forall \left(k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\left\lVert \psi\left(k\right) \right\rVert = \left(1: \mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right) \land \left(\forall \left(i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\left(i \ne j\right) \to \left(\left(\left(\{i, j\}: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right)\right) \ne \left(\{i_{0}, j_{0}\}: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right)\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.overlap}\left(\psi\left(i\right), \psi\left(j\right)\right) = r\left(i, j\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.realizes` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A family ψ realizes the given values when each vector has norm one and every ordered pair of distinct indices has overlap r i j, except when its unordered two-element finite set equals the unknown pair. Thus both orientations of the unknown pair are omitted, and diagonal values of r impose no conditions. The predicate permits arbitrary n, m, i₀, j₀ and r, without separately requiring symmetry of r or distinctness of i₀ and j₀.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (All feasible values of the unknown overlap).**
+
+$$\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.feasible}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right): \operatorname{Set}\left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right) = \{\left(t: \mathbb{R}\right) \mid \left(\exists \left(n: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\exists \left(\psi: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.realizes}\left(i_{0}, j_{0}, r, \psi\right)\right) \land \left(t = \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.overlap}\left(\psi\left(i_{0}\right), \psi\left(j_{0}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\}\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.feasible` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The feasible set consists of the real values t realized as the unknown squared overlap by some normalized family satisfying every given pair. Both the natural dimension n and the family ψ are existentially quantified, so no fixed dimension is assumed.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Intersection of the lower bounds).**
+
+$$\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procLower}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \operatorname{sSup}\left(\{\left(t: \mathbb{R}\right) \mid \left(\exists \left(k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\left(k \ne i_{0}\right) \land \left(\left(k \ne j_{0}\right) \land \left(t = \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.lower}\left(r\left(k, i_{0}\right), r\left(k, j_{0}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procLower` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every k distinct from i₀ and j₀, apply the three-state lower bound to r k i₀ and r k j₀, then take the supremum of the resulting set. This is the lower endpoint of the common-neighbour intersection in overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 151–154, for a graph with only the pair i₀,j₀ unknown. For m at least three the finite set is nonempty and its supremum is its maximum. The definition also includes smaller m through the real supremum operation.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Intersection of the upper bounds).**
+
+$$\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procUpper}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \operatorname{sInf}\left(\{\left(t: \mathbb{R}\right) \mid \left(\exists \left(k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\left(k \ne i_{0}\right) \land \left(\left(k \ne j_{0}\right) \land \left(t = \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.upper}\left(r\left(k, i_{0}\right), r\left(k, j_{0}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procUpper` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Apply the three-state upper bound through each common neighbour k and take the infimum of those values. This is the upper endpoint of the intersection in overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 151–154, for one unknown pair. For m at least three the finite nonempty set has a minimum; the definition uses the real infimum operation for every m.
+
+**Definition 1.8 (Universal tightness with one unknown pair).**
+
+$$\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.claim}\right) \Leftrightarrow \left(\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\left(3: \mathbb{N}\right) \le m\right) \to \left(\left(i_{0} \ne j_{0}\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Set.Nonempty}\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.feasible}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right)\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procLower}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right) = \operatorname{sInf}\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.feasible}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right)\right)\right) \land \left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procUpper}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right) = \operatorname{sSup}\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.feasible}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+

+# A symmetric injective matrix-product family with four physical levels
+
+## Abstract
+
+Four physical levels with nonzero charge values admit a normalized, symmetric matrix-product family of bond dimension three that is injective at block length two.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Periodic matrix-product amplitudes).**
+
+$$\forall \left(d: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(a: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right), \mathbb{C}\right)\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(n: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(w: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.SpinChains.FourLevelU1SymmetricInjectiveMPS.amplitude}\left(a, n, w\right): \mathbb{C}\right) = \operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.SourceJetCyclicTraces.orderedTraceWord}\left(\left(\lambda \left(i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right) \mapsto \left(a\left(w\left(i\right)\right)\right)\right), \operatorname{id}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$

The identity ordering retains the order of the sites; at n = 0 the empty product is the identity matrix.

+

+# Original lattice discriminant S, Weil and Milgram laws
+
+## Abstract
+
+The literal shifted theta series of every positive even integral lattice transforms by its actual discriminant pairing. Negative Fourier operators on all functions satisfy the phased Weil relations, and the original positive Gaussian fixes the Milgram phase. All natural ranks are included. No fusion, Monster, sewing, CFT, string or AdS realization is asserted.
+
+The three theorem statements are classical: Borcherds, Section 4, Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2. The cited Library note maps the original Gram cokernel to the lattice discriminant and checks the signs and principal branch. His finite S operator is exp(-pi i rank/4) times the unphased S defined here, while his T has the same positive quadratic sign. The repository authors the Lean derivations, including the theta-orbit proof of Milgram; it does not claim authorship of these statements.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Positive cardinal normalization).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.rho`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.rho` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The scalar rho is the complex cast of the positive real square root of the cardinality of the actual Gram cokernel. Positivity of the original real Gram matrix identifies its square with det G and makes rho nonzero.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Negative Fourier operator).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.weilS`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.weilS` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+On every complex function f on the original discriminant A, S f at a is rho inverse times the sum over b of exp(-2 pi i B(a,b)) f(b). This is a complex linear endomorphism on the whole function space.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Positive Fourier inverse).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.weilSplus`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.weilSplus` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The positive Fourier operator has kernel exp(+2 pi i B(a,b)) divided by rho. It is both a left and a right inverse of the negative operator on every function.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Original half-norm operator).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.weilT`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.weilT` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The complex linear operator T multiplies f(a) by exp(2 pi i q(a)), where q is the half norm of the original even integral Gram lattice modulo integers.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Charge conjugation).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.chargeConjugation`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.chargeConjugation` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The complex linear operator C sends f(a) to f(-a) on every complex function. No evenness assumption is imposed on f.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Positive normalized Gauss sum).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.gaussPhase`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.gaussPhase` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For the actual finite discriminant, gamma is rho inverse times the sum of exp(+2 pi i q(a)) over every class a. The positive sign is part of this definition.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (All original shifted sectors under inversion).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.sector_S`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.sector_S` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Richard E. Borcherds (1998). *Automorphic forms with singularities on Grassmannians*. DOI: [10.1007/s002220050232](https://doi.org/10.1007/s002220050232).
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every original LatticeData D with positive real Gram matrix, every discriminant class a and every tau with positive imaginary part, Theta_a(-1/tau) equals (-i tau) to the principal power rank/2, divided by sqrt(det G), times the sum over c of exp(-2 pi i B(a,c)) Theta_c(tau). Coordinate Poisson summation applies to the literal translated Gaussian. Translation has a positive Fourier phase; integer negation converts the absolutely convergent dual sum to the existing negative inverse coefficient. Compact normal convergence is transported through the translated compact set, including empty sets and rank zero.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (Full function-space Weil identities).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.finite_weil_relations`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.finite_weil_relations` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Richard E. Borcherds (1998). *Automorphic forms with singularities on Grassmannians*. DOI: [10.1007/s002220050232](https://doi.org/10.1007/s002220050232).
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every original positive even integral lattice, rho is nonzero and rho squared is the discriminant cardinality. On the whole complex function space, S squared equals C, S to the fourth equals the identity, and both products S Splus and Splus S equal the identity. With composition S after T, (S T) cubed equals gamma C. Character orthogonality and a finite completed-square identity prove these relations independently of theta values. These are phased relations; they do not assert an unphased modular representation or isometry for the supremum norm.
+
+**Theorem 1.9 (Milgram phase of the original positive even lattice).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.milgram`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/VertexAlgebra/Characters/LatticeDiscriminantWeil.milgram` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* Richard E. Borcherds (1998). *Automorphic forms with singularities on Grassmannians*. DOI: [10.1007/s002220050232](https://doi.org/10.1007/s002220050232).
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural rank, the positive normalized Gauss sum of the original positive even integral Gram lattice equals exp(pi i rank/4). The actual theta S and T transformations along i, (-1+i)/2, -1+i and i combine with the full-space cubic relation. The principal logs of 1-i and (1-i)/2 add to Log(-i), giving exp(-pi i rank/4) for the product of weight factors. Representative independence identifies the original zero sector at i with a convergent positive real Gaussian sum; its zero-vector term is one, so its real part is at least one. Cancelling this nonzero original theta value fixes the positive phase. No positive-rank, even-rank or diagonal restriction is imposed.

+# Unconditional integrated explicit formula
+
+## Abstract
+
+Unconditional integrated explicit formula
+
+For every real y>0, the complete actual zero occurrence series equals U(exp(y))-log(2*pi) plus the full trivial zero correction. The residual is literally zero on y<=0 and damped by exp(-2*y) on y>0. Its L1 Fourier transform vanishes at nonzero frequencies by the actual Laplace suppliers. Continuity of that transform gives frequency zero without applying the digamma series at integer one. Pointwise inversion uses continuity only at the requested positive y. This formula makes no RH, Robin positivity or positive U peak claim. Integer 5040, all integer endpoints N>=2, every prime-power endpoint and the literal exponential-over-denominator form are checked only by transient anonymous applications.

+theorem fixed_count_prodMap (f : X → X) (g : Y → Y) [Fintype X] [Fintype Y]
+    (n : ℕ) :
+    fixedCount (Prod.map f g) n = fixedCount f n * fixedCount g n := by
+  classical
+  unfold fixedCount
+  rw [← Fintype.card_subtype, ← Fintype.card_subtype, ← Fintype.card_subtype]
+  let e :
+      {x : X × Y // (Prod.map f g)^[n] x = x} ≃
+        ({x : X // f^[n] x = x} × {y : Y // g^[n] y = y}) :=
+    { toFun := fun z =>
+        let hz : f^[n] z.1.1 = z.1.1 ∧ g^[n] z.1.2 = z.1.2 := by
+          have hz' := z.2
+          have hi := congrArg (fun h : (X × Y) → X × Y => h z.1)
+            (Prod.map_iterate f g n)
+          have hp := hi.symm.trans hz'
+          change (f^[n] z.1.1, g^[n] z.1.2) = z.1 at hp
+          exact Prod.ext_iff.mp hp
+        ⟨⟨z.1.1, hz.1⟩, ⟨z.1.2, hz.2⟩⟩
+      invFun := fun z =>
+        ⟨(z.1.1, z.2.1), by
+          have hi := congrArg (fun h : (X × Y) → X × Y => h (z.1.1, z.2.1))
+            (Prod.map_iterate f g n)
+          have hr : Prod.map (f^[n]) (g^[n]) (z.1.1, z.2.1) =
+              (z.1.1, z.2.1) := by
+            change (f^[n] z.1.1, g^[n] z.2.1) = (z.1.1, z.2.1)
+            exact Prod.ext_iff.mpr ⟨z.1.2, z.2.2⟩
+          exact hi.trans hr⟩
+      left_inv := by
+        intro z
+        exact Subtype.ext rfl
+      right_inv := by
+        intro z
+        exact Prod.ext (Subtype.ext rfl) (Subtype.ext rfl) }

+namespace D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Geometry.BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup

+open BiasedBoundaryTrace (G M J Omega cylinder indicator)

+private theorem prefixes_step (p : Address) (b : Bool) :
+    prefixes (p ++ [b]) = insert ⟨p ++ [b], by simp⟩ (prefixes p) := by
+  classical
+  ext q
+  simp [prefixes, List.inits_append, Subtype.ext_iff, or_comm]
+
+private theorem prefix_step (p : Address) (b : Bool) (z : H) :
+    prefixSum (p ++ [b]) z = prefixSum p z + z ⟨p ++ [b], by simp⟩ := by
+  classical
+  rw [boundary_path_split.2.2.1, prefixes_step, Finset.sum_insert]
+  · rw [boundary_path_split.2.2.1]
+    ring
+  · intro h
+    have hpre : (p ++ [b]).IsPrefix p := by
+      simpa [prefixes, List.mem_inits] using h
+    have := hpre.length_le
+    simp at this
+
+/-- The actual rooted potential, including its free real root value. -/
+def potential (c : ℝ) (z : H) (p : Address) : ℝ := c + prefixSum p z
+
+private theorem potential_step (c : ℝ) (z : H) (p : Address) (b : Bool) :
+    potential c z (p ++ [b]) = potential c z p + z ⟨p ++ [b], by simp⟩ := by
+  simp only [potential, prefix_step]
+  ring
+
+private theorem potential_increment (c : ℝ) (z : H) (p : Edge) :
+    potential c z p.val - potential c z p.val.dropLast = z p := by
+  have h : ∀ (q : Address) (hq : q ≠ []),
+      potential c z q - potential c z q.dropLast = z ⟨q,hq⟩ := by
+    intro q
+    induction q using List.reverseRecOn with
+    | nil => simp
+    | append_singleton q b ih =>
+      intro hq
+      rw [List.dropLast_concat, potential_step]
+      ring
+  exact h p.val p.property
+
+/-- Increment of the contracted actual potential along an original edge. -/
+def contractedCoordinate (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (z : H) (p : Edge) : ℝ :=
+  χ (potential c z p.val) - χ (potential c z p.val.dropLast)
+
+private theorem contracted_bound (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ)
+    (c : ℝ) (z : H) (p : Edge) : ‖contractedCoordinate χ c z p‖ ≤ ‖z p‖ := by
+  have h := hχ.norm_sub_le (potential c z p.val) (potential c z p.val.dropLast)
+  simpa only [contractedCoordinate, NNReal.coe_one, one_mul, potential_increment] using h
+
+/-- Square-summable increments after contraction of the actual rooted potential. -/
+def contracted (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (c : ℝ) (z : H) : H :=
+  ⟨contractedCoordinate χ c z,
+    (lp.memℓp z).mono' (contracted_bound χ hχ c z)⟩
+
+private theorem contracted_prefix (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ)
+    (c : ℝ) (z : H) (p : Address) :
+    potential (χ c) (contracted χ hχ c z) p = χ (potential c z p) := by
+  induction p using List.reverseRecOn with
+  | nil =>
+    have he : prefixes [] = ∅ := by
+      ext q
+      simp [prefixes, q.property]
+    simp [potential, prefixSum, he]
+  | append_singleton p b ih =>
+    rw [potential_step, ih]
+    change χ (potential c z p) +
+      (χ (potential c z (p ++ [b])) - χ (potential c z (p ++ [b]).dropLast)) = _
+    rw [List.dropLast_concat]
+    ring
+
+/-- Every real normal contraction acts on the original all-edge extension with
+no increase of increment energy, and its exact potential agrees at every vertex.
+The root is transformed freely; no condition on the image of zero is required. -/
+private theorem contracted_extension (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ)
+    (c : ℝ) (z : H) :
+    (∀ p : Edge, contracted χ hχ c z p =
+      χ (potential c z p.val) - χ (potential c z p.val.dropLast)) ∧
+    ‖contracted χ hχ c z‖ ≤ ‖z‖ ∧
+    (∀ p : Address, potential (χ c) (contracted χ hχ c z) p =
+      χ (potential c z p)) := by
+  refine ⟨fun _ => rfl, ?_, contracted_prefix χ hχ c z⟩
+  exact lp.norm_mono (by norm_num : (2 : ENNReal) ≠ 0) (contracted_bound χ hχ c z)

+  classical

+    Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_range]
+  constructor

+    rw [← hw, List.length_ofFn]
+    omega
+  · intro hp
+    exact ⟨p.val.length, by omega, p.val.get, List.ofFn_get p.val⟩

+private theorem cutoff_expansion (h : ℕ) (z : H) :
+    P h z = ∑ p ∈ cutoff h, lp.single 2 p (z p) := by
+  classical
+  rw [FiniteSourceCovariance.P_expand]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr
+  · ext p
+    change p ∈ ((List.finite_length_le Bool h).toFinset).subtype (· ≠ []) ↔ p ∈ cutoff h
+    simp [mem_cutoff]
+  · intro p hp
+    change (z p • lp.single 2 p (1 : ℝ) : H) = lp.single 2 p (z p)
+    rw [← lp.single_smul]

+private theorem ray_prefix_iff (ω : Omega) (h : ℕ) (p : Edge) :
+    p.val.IsPrefix (D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix ω h) ↔
+      p.val.length ≤ h ∧ ω ∈ cylinder p.val := by
+  constructor
+  · intro hp
+    have hl : p.val.length ≤ h := by
+      simpa [D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix] using hp.length_le
+    refine ⟨hl, (BiasedBoundaryCylinderProjection.cylinder_ray _ _).mpr ?_⟩
+    apply List.ext_getElem (by simp [D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix])

+    have he := hp.getElem hi
+    simpa [D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix] using he
+  · rintro ⟨hl,hω⟩
+    rw [(BiasedBoundaryCylinderProjection.cylinder_ray _ _).mp hω]
+    apply List.prefix_iff_getElem.mpr
+    refine ⟨by simpa [D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix] using hl, ?_⟩
+    intro i hi
+    simp [D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix]
+
+private theorem cutoff_trace (h : ℕ) (z : H) :
+    J (P h z) =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => prefixSum
+      (D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix ω h) z) := by
+  classical
+  rw [cutoff_expansion, map_sum]
+  simp_rw [BiasedBoundaryTrace.J_single]
+  have hi : ∀ᵐ ω ∂M, ∀ p : Edge,
+      indicator p ω = (cylinder p.val).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω :=
+    ae_all_iff.mpr (fun _ => indicatorConstLp_coeFn)
+  have hm : ∀ᵐ ω ∂M, ∀ p : Edge,
+      (z p • indicator p : G) ω = z p * indicator p ω :=
+    ae_all_iff.mpr (fun p => Lp.coeFn_smul (z p) (indicator p))
+  filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_finsetSum (cutoff h) (fun p => z p • indicator p), hi, hm]
+    with ω hs hi hm
+  rw [hs, boundary_path_split.2.2.1]
+  simp only [Finset.sum_apply]

+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, mem_cutoff, prefixes, Finset.mem_subtype,
+      List.mem_toFinset, List.mem_inits]
+    exact (ray_prefix_iff ω h p).symm
+  rw [← he, Finset.sum_filter]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro p hp
+  rw [hm p, hi p]

+
+private theorem projection_tendsto (z : H) : Tendsto (fun h : ℕ => P h z) atTop (𝓝 z) := by
+  have hc : Tendsto cutoff atTop atTop := by
+    apply tendsto_atTop.mpr
+    intro s
+    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (s.sup (fun p : Edge => p.val.length))] with h hh
+    intro p hp
+    exact (mem_cutoff h p).mpr ((Finset.le_sup hp).trans hh)
+  have hs := (lp.hasSum_single (by norm_num : (2 : ENNReal) ≠ ⊤) z).comp hc
+  simpa only [Function.comp_def, ← cutoff_expansion] using hs

+private theorem shifted_lipschitz (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) :
+    LipschitzWith 1 (fun x => χ x - χ 0) := by
+  apply LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul
+  intro x y
+  simpa only [dist_eq_norm, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using hχ.dist_le_mul x y

+/-- Composition on the actual probability L2 space, without requiring χ(0)=0. -/
+def contractLp (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : G) : G :=
+  constG (χ 0) + (shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).compLp (by simp) F
+
+private theorem contractLp_ae (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : G) :
+    contractLp χ hχ F =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => χ (F ω)) := by
+  filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_add (constG (χ 0)) ((shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).compLp (by simp) F),
+    boundary_path_split.2.2.2.1 (χ 0),
+    (shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).coeFn_compLp (by simp) F] with ω ha hc hf
+  change (constG (χ 0) + (shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).compLp (by simp) F) ω = _
+  rw [ha, Pi.add_apply, hc, hf]
+  change χ 0 + (χ (F ω) - χ 0) = _
+  ring
+
+private theorem depth_ae (c : ℝ) (z : H) (h : ℕ) :
+    constG c + J (P h z) =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => potential c z
+      (D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix ω h)) := by
+  filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_add (constG c) (J (P h z)),
+    boundary_path_split.2.2.2.1 c, cutoff_trace h z] with ω ha hc hz
+  rw [ha, Pi.add_apply, hc, hz]
+  rfl
+
+private theorem trace_compatibility (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ)
+    (c : ℝ) (z : H) :
+    contractLp χ hχ (constG c + J z) = constG (χ c) + J (contracted χ hχ c z) := by
+  have hc : Continuous (contractLp χ hχ : G → G) :=
+    continuous_const.add ((shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).continuous_compLp (by simp))
+  have hlim (d : ℝ) (w : H) :
+      Tendsto (fun h : ℕ => constG d + J (P h w)) atTop (𝓝 (constG d + J w)) :=
+    tendsto_const_nhds.add (J.continuous.continuousAt.tendsto.comp (projection_tendsto w))
+  have he (h : ℕ) : contractLp χ hχ (constG c + J (P h z)) =
+      constG (χ c) + J (P h (contracted χ hχ c z)) := by
+    apply Lp.ext
+    filter_upwards [contractLp_ae χ hχ (constG c + J (P h z)),
+      depth_ae c z h, depth_ae (χ c) (contracted χ hχ c z) h] with ω hχ hF hG
+    rw [hχ, hF, hG, contracted_prefix]
+  exact tendsto_nhds_unique ((hc.continuousAt.tendsto.comp (hlim c z)).congr he)

+
+/-- The contracted original-edge extension has an actual trace in the original
+free-root domain. Its energy is no larger than that of the least extension of F,
+and its value at every finite vertex is the contracted original potential. -/
+private theorem contracted_trace_candidate (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : D) :
+    ∃ (c : ℝ) (w : H),
+      F.val = constG c + J (BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F) ∧
+      w = contracted χ hχ c (BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F) ∧
+      constG (χ c) + J w ∈ D ∧
+      energy (constG (χ c) + J w) ≤ energy F.val ∧
+      (∀ p : Address, potential (χ c) w p =
+        χ (potential c (BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F) p)) := by
+  let z := BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F
+  let c := BiasedBoundaryCentering.mean F.val - BiasedBoundaryCentering.mean (J z)
+  let w := contracted χ hχ c z

+  have hm : constG (χ c) + J w ∈ D := ⟨χ c, w, rfl⟩
+  have hw := contracted_extension χ hχ c z
+  refine ⟨c, w, he.2.2.1, rfl, hm, ?_, hw.2.2⟩
+  have hb := (free_root_least_energy ⟨constG (χ c) + J w, hm⟩).2.2.2.2.1
+    (χ c) w rfl
+  calc
+    energy (constG (χ c) + J w) =
+        ‖BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift ⟨constG (χ c) + J w, hm⟩‖^2 :=
+      (free_root_least_energy ⟨constG (χ c) + J w, hm⟩).2.2.2.1
+    _ ≤ ‖w‖^2 := hb.2
+    _ ≤ ‖z‖^2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) hw.2.1 2
+    _ = energy F.val := he.2.2.2.1.symm
+
+/-- Every real one-Lipschitz map preserves the actual free-root trace domain
+and decreases its original infimum energy on the actual biased probability law. -/
+theorem actual_trace_contraction (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : D) :
+    (contractLp χ hχ F.val =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => χ (F.val ω))) ∧
+    contractLp χ hχ F.val ∈ D ∧ energy (contractLp χ hχ F.val) ≤ energy F.val := by
+  obtain ⟨c,w,hF,hw,hm,hen,_⟩ := contracted_trace_candidate χ hχ F
+  refine ⟨contractLp_ae χ hχ F.val, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rw [hF, trace_compatibility, ← hw]
+    exact hm
+  · rw [hF, trace_compatibility, ← hw]
+    simpa only [← hF] using hen

+#print axioms contracted_trace_candidate

+noncomputable section
+namespace D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Geometry.FiniteSourceScreening

+open ActualTreeReadoutAcquisition (Address)
+open FiniteSourceHardy (H NodeL2)
+open FiniteSourceMass (N)
+open FiniteSourceCovariance (one v B Sigma)
